message_source_quote: This is the **same mechanism** white-bear steering (Raman et al. 2026) identified — a stance push at the concept-allocation band that the blocks above carry into the read position.

differences.writeup_quote: All of them were flat or harmful (pass@10 ≤ 0.14, i.e. at or below baseline), consistent with WBS's note that content directions do not reach the per-item retrieval process.
differences.what: The write-up explicitly attributes an additional corroborating finding to WBS (that content directions don't reach the per-item retrieval process) to explain why only the stance direction worked; the message reports the same failed screens but omits this attribution to the source.

rationale: Both documents credit Raman et al. (2026) / white-bear steering identically: same mechanism, same geometry confirmation, same cosine figures (0.86–0.88 vs ≥0.997 leave-one-out), and the same novelty claim that the stance direction is not pinned to the directed_modulation family and does not collapse onto a single layer like WBS's does. The only notable gap is that the write-up also credits WBS with a broader explanatory claim (that content directions generally don't reach the per-item retrieval process) to interpret the screening results, which the message's summary of the same screening table does not mention.
